candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: afterMedia
candidates.comment: An after media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL depicting the state or circumstances after completing that step. Also called post-step media, result image, outcome visual. Examples: "A recipe direction's after media is an image of the mixed ingredients.", "The assembly instruction's after media is a video of the connected parts."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: follows
candidates.comment: A follows relation representing a generic uni-directional social connection between two people. Also called: is following, subscribes to, tracks. Examples: "Alice follows Bob", "Charlie follows David", "Eve follows Frank". Distinct from followee, which is the object of a follow action.

candidates.label: followee
candidates.comment: A followee relation between a follow action and the person or organization that is being followed. Also called: followed entity, subject of follow, target of follow. Examples: "User A follows User B" followee "User B", "Fan follows Band X" followee "Band X", "Journalist follows News Organization Y" followee "News Organization Y". Distinct from follows, which is the general social relation.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: associatedArticle
candidates.comment: A news article linked to a media object. Also called: related article, accompanying article, news story link. Examples: "MediaObject 'Video of Protest' associatedArticle 'NewsArticle on Protest'", "MediaObject 'Photo of Event' associatedArticle 'Article about Event'."

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: holdingArchive
candidates.comment: A holding archive relation between an archive component and the archive organization that maintains it. Also called maintained by, kept by, archive holder. Examples: "An archive component has a holding archive 'National Archives'.", "The document is part of a holding archive.", "This record is held by a specific holding archive."

candidates.label: archiveHeld
candidates.comment: An archive held relation between an archive organization and a collection, fonds, or item maintained by it. Also called archival holding, collection maintained, item preserved. Examples: "The National Archives' archive held is 'Presidential Papers'.", "The historical society's archive held is 'Local Family Records'."

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: containsPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and another smaller place that it contains. Also called "includes place", "encompasses", "holds". Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: catalog
candidates.comment: A containment relation between a dataset and the data catalog that holds it. Also called "contained in catalog", "part of catalog", "dataset catalog". Examples: "Census data dataset catalog National Data Archive", "Research dataset catalog University Data Repository".

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: acceptsReservations
candidates.comment: A reservation acceptance status indicating whether a food establishment allows bookings. Also called takes reservations, booking available, reservation policy. Examples: "A restaurant accepts reservations is true.", "The cafe accepts reservations via its website URL.", "This diner accepts reservations is 'No'."

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: playMode
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the supported gameplay modes for a video game or series, such as single-player, multi-player, or co-op. Also called game mode, player configuration, gameplay style. Examples: A video game has a play mode of 'SinglePlayer'. A video game has a play mode of 'MultiPlayer'. candidates.label: characterName
candidates.comment: A naming relation for a performance role, indicating the name of the character being played. Also called "role name", "played character", "fictional name". Examples: "Actor's performance role characterName 'Hamlet'", "Actress's performance role characterName 'Juliet'". Distinct from character, which refers to the fictional person itself, whereas characterName is the name of the character in a specific performance.

candidates.label: sport
candidates.comment: An identification of the type of sport associated with a sports event or organization. Also called "sport type", "athletic discipline", "game played". Examples: "The event's sport is Basketball", "The organization's sport is Soccer", "This competition features the sport of Gymnastics."

candidates.label: game
candidates.comment: A game relation between a game server and the video game that is hosted and played on it. Also called: hosted game, server game, game played. Examples: "Minecraft Server" game "Minecraft", "World of Warcraft Realm" game "World of Warcraft", "CS:GO Server" game "Counter-Strike: Global Offensive".

candidates.label: actor
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) or event and a person or performing group who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actor is 'Tom Hanks'.", "A play's actor is 'The Ensemble Theatre'.", "An episode's actor is 'Jane Doe'." Distinct from actors, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.

candidates.label: numberOfPlayers
candidates.comment: The number of people who can play a game or video game series, often expressed as a minimum, maximum, or range. Also called player count, game capacity, participant number. Examples: "Board Game X numberOfPlayers '2-4'", "Video Game Y numberOfPlayers '1 (single-player)'", "Online Game Z numberOfPlayers '100 (max)'".

candidates.label: gameServer
candidates.comment: A game server relation between a video game and the server where it can be played. Also called: hosted on, playable server, game host. Examples: "Minecraft" game server "Hypixel Network", "World of Warcraft" game server "Frostmourne Realm", "Call of Duty" game server "Dedicated Server". Distinct from game, which is the game itself.

candidates.label: playerType
candidates.comment: A technical attribute indicating the specific media player type required to render a media object. Also called required player, media renderer, playback software. Examples: A video file has a player type of 'Flash'. A media object has a player type of 'Silverlight'. An audio stream has a player type of 'HTML5 Audio'.

candidates.label: actors
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) and a person who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actors include 'Brad Pitt'.", "An episode's actors include 'Jennifer Aniston'." Distinct from actor, which is the preferred and more general property that also allows PerformingGroup.

candidates.label: awayTeam
candidates.comment: A person or sports team designated as the away team in a sports event. Also called: visiting team, opponent. Examples: "SportsEvent 'Football Match' awayTeam 'Team B'", "SportsEvent 'Basketball Game' awayTeam 'Lakers'". Distinct from homeTeam, which is the team playing at their home venue.
